decision_table.name: Determine_SD_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file South Dakota corporate tax return. South Dakota has NO corporate income tax - no filing required.

condition.name: is_general_corporation
condition.comment: General business corporation (not financial institution or insurance company)

condition.name: is_financial_institution
condition.comment: Financial institution subject to Bank Franchise Tax

condition.name: is_insurance_company
condition.comment: Insurance company subject to Insurance Premium Tax

rule.policy:
South Dakota has NO corporate income tax.
South Dakota is one of the few states with truly NO corporate taxation: - NO corporate income tax - NO franchise tax (unlike Texas) - NO gross receipts tax (unlike Nevada) - NO commerce tax - NO alternative minimum tax - NO filing requirement for general business corporations
Historical Context: South Dakota brought the landmark case South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018), which established economic nexus standards for sales tax nationwide. Despite this, South Dakota has NO corporate income tax.
Why No Corporate Income Tax? South Dakota relies on sales tax, property tax, and other revenue sources instead of income taxation. This makes South Dakota attractive for business incorporation and operation.
Any estimated tax payments made in error would be refunded.
Reference: South Dakota Constitution Article XI § 2 - Income tax prohibited Reference: SDCL Title 10 - Taxation (no corporate income tax chapter exists) Reference: South Dakota Department of Revenue - No corporate income tax Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018)

South Dakota Bank Franchise Tax (financial institutions ONLY).
IMPORTANT: This is NOT a corporate income tax.
South Dakota imposes a Bank Franchise Tax on financial institutions (banks, trust companies, savings and loans, credit unions) based on their net income or capital/surplus.
This is a specialized tax that applies ONLY to financial institutions, NOT to general business corporations.
General corporations do NOT pay this tax.
Bank Franchise Tax calculation is not implemented in this system (requires specialized financial institution tax software).
Reference: SDCL 10-43 - Bank Franchise Tax Reference: SDCL 10-43-3 - Rate and calculation Reference: South Dakota Department of Revenue - Bank Franchise Tax Guide

South Dakota Insurance Premium Tax (insurance companies ONLY).
IMPORTANT: This is NOT a corporate income tax.
South Dakota imposes an Insurance Premium Tax on insurance companies based on premiums collected in South Dakota.
This is a specialized tax that applies ONLY to insurance companies, NOT to general business corporations.
General corporations do NOT pay this tax.
Insurance Premium Tax calculation is not implemented in this system (requires specialized insurance tax software).
Reference: SDCL 10-44 - Insurance Premium Tax Reference: SDCL 10-44-2 - Rate and calculation Reference: South Dakota Department of Revenue - Insurance Premium Tax

decision_table.name: Calculate_SD_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: South Dakota has NO corporate income tax. This table confirms zero income tax liability for consistency with framework.

rule.policy:
South Dakota has NO corporate income tax.
South Dakota does NOT tax corporate net income. There are: - NO state income tax adjustments (no additions or subtractions) - NO apportionment of federal taxable income - NO state tax rate (rate is 0.0%) - NO state taxable income calculation - NO filing requirement for general corporations
This decision table confirms zero income tax for framework consistency.
Note: South Dakota DOES have sales tax (4.5% state rate) which applies to retail sales, but that is a completely separate tax system and NOT a corporate income tax.
Reference: South Dakota Constitution Article XI § 2 - Income tax prohibited Reference: SDCL Title 10 - Taxation (no corporate income tax chapter) Reference: South Dakota has no corporate income tax statute (intentionally)

Specialized entity (financial institution or insurance company).
These entities are subject to specialized taxes (Bank Franchise Tax, Insurance Premium Tax) but these are NOT corporate income taxes.
No adjustments to federal taxable income are made.

South Dakota has NO corporate income tax.

IMPORTANT: South Dakota is one of the few states with truly NO corporate taxation for general business corporations:
NO Corporate Income Tax: - South Dakota does not tax corporate net income - No filing requirement for general corporations - No apportionment calculation needed - No state-specific income adjustments
NO Alternative Corporate Taxes: - NO franchise tax (unlike Texas) - NO gross receipts tax (unlike Ohio CAT) - NO commerce tax (unlike Nevada) - NO alternative minimum tax
Why No Corporate Income Tax? South Dakota relies on other revenue sources instead: - Sales and Use Tax: 4.5% state rate (on retail sales, NOT corporate income) - Property Tax: Local property taxes on real and personal property - Special taxes: Specific to certain industries (banks, insurance, etc.)
Business-Friendly Environment: South Dakota's lack of corporate income tax makes it an attractive state for business incorporation, headquarters location, and operations.
Historical Note: Despite bringing the landmark Wayfair case (establishing economic nexus for sales tax), South Dakota maintains its policy of no corporate income tax.
Refunds: Any South Dakota estimated tax payments made in error will be refunded.
